A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UniWM, despite the revised title and presentation. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching of retained and added content.

before.justification: v1 reports original navigation and visualization experiments on four training/evaluation datasets, zero-shot TartanDrive results, ablations, and qualitative examples.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds humanoid navigation results, further controlled ablations, an Aether comparison, and inference-time results.

M1.justification: v2 reports a limited action-interface extension: a separate UniWM instance uses 25-DoF humanoid joint-angle actions instead of the original translation/yaw commands (Sections 4.1 and 4.5). The backbone, losses, hierarchical memory, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. The humanoid adaptation is not described in implementation-level detail.

E1.justification: v2 adds training and evaluation on the navigation subset of the 1X Humanoid Dataset, extending coverage to humanoid embodiment and high-dimensional joint-angle control. The original four navigation datasets and held-out TartanDrive coverage are retained.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds Aether to the visualization comparison, which previously contained Diamond and NWM. v2 specifies checkpoint-based evaluation because Aether lacks released training code and uses an incompatible camera-pose action space. The navigation comparator set is unchanged, including when extended to humanoid evaluation.

E3.justification: v2 adds a separately trained humanoid setting with 6599/733 training/evaluation trajectories, a joint-versus-separate training control using identical data and schedules, a retrained goal-image removal control, and per-trajectory latency evaluation. Existing dataset splits, preprocessing, navigation/visualization metrics, and the 20-epoch LoRA setup remain unchanged. Newly stated baseline-retraining information does not establish a change to the original experiments.

E4.justification: v2 adds direct tests of joint versus separate planner/world-model training (Table 4) and whether goal conditioning affects unseen-environment generalization (Section 4.3). Appendix B.2 adds an inference-cost analysis, and Figure 4 adds a moving-pedestrian qualitative case. The original loss, context, memory, layer-selection, and interleaving ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new estimated 4-bit latency is a point projection, not statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Matched original tables and Figure 5 retain their values. v2 adds Aether scores, humanoid results, ablation outcomes, latency results, and qualitative findings. For example, Table 8 reports humanoid SR 0.81 for full UniWM versus 0.51 for NWM; Table 4 reports SR 0.71 for unified versus 0.65 for separate training. Table A1 reports 82 seconds per UniWM trajectory and explicitly labels the 16-second quantized figure as estimated.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, losses, memory-fusion equations, attention equation, and appendix metric definitions are retained. v1 Equation 12 becomes v2 Equation A1 without substantive revision. Neither version adds theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion newly claim scalability to high-dimensional humanoid control. The central contributions—unified planning and imagination, interleaved training, and hierarchical memory—remain intact, as do the original navigation and zero-shot generalization claims.

C2.justification: v2 newly interprets goal conditioning as helping unseen-environment generalization and discusses the accuracy-versus-imagination-cost tradeoff, including potential quantization benefits. The domain-shift and fixed-token-budget limitations remain; the explanation of disappearing ego-robot regions is slightly qualified from absent to rare training examples.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents baseline retraining on the shared datasets and Aether's checkpoint-only exception, and expands the abstract's availability statement from code to code and models. Most implementation details and appendix prompts are retained, but the explicit per-GPU batch size of 1 and gradient accumulation of 2 are omitted. These documentation changes do not establish altered original training settings.

R1.justification: v2 adds contemporary world-model, driving, humanoid, and quantization references, plus targeted distinctions from MVoT's narrow 2D reasoning and WorldVLA's single-step action-sequence prediction without trajectory memory. These refine the novelty discussion while retaining the original positioning around unified prediction/control and structured memory.

P1.justification: v2 extensively edits the introduction and experimental narrative, changes the title and author/affiliation information, moves related work from Appendix A into main Section 2, introduces an explicit experimental-settings subsection, and places references after the appendices. Existing appendix methods and metrics are reorganized rather than removed.

P2.justification: v2 redesigns the title block, typography, colors, table styling, and framework diagrams in Figures 1–3. It adds Tables 4, 8, and A1, a humanoid Figure 7, and an additional Figure 4 case. Original appendix figures are retained as Figures A1–A5 with revised placement and formatting.

improvement.justification: v1 lacked a matched test isolating joint from separate planner/world-model training; v2 Table 4 addresses this central attribution gap. Together with the goal-conditioning control, humanoid evaluation, baseline-training disclosures, and inference-cost analysis, this substantially strengthens the paper's empirical support and assessability. The gains are qualified by sparse humanoid-adaptation and timing details, omitted batch-scheduling details, and the explicitly estimated rather than measured 4-bit latency.
